applied.problem: 'A breaker opens within the time only once the current reaches Ia' is too absolute: a type B can trip instantly from 3 In and a type C from 5 In, below their Ia; Ia is the current at which opening in time is certain.

Screens 2 and 3 say a current below Ia is too small to open the device in time and that it opens in time only at Ia, but the picture's own 'May trip' band (125 to 250 A) shows it may; and Table 41.5 is not in the BS 7671 pages Dan holds (p.441 to 491).
Says a breaker below Ia opens only on its thermal part and too late; between 5 and 10 In a type C may still trip instantly (the picture's 'May trip' band), so lateness is possible, not certain.
'Opens in time only if the current reaches Ia' is too absolute: a breaker can trip instantly below Ia (a type B from 3 In); Ia is the current that makes opening in time certain.
Same overstatement as the point: a device can open in time below Ia; reaching Ia is what makes it certain.

The 722.411.4.1 methods are balanced loading, an earth electrode at the installation, or an open-PEN device; making the point TT is a separate option that takes it off the PME earth altogether, not one of those methods.
A device that detects DC fault current is used with a Type A or F RCD, not on its own; the research gives a Type B RCD, or a Type A or F with a DC-detecting device.
Carries the same two slips as points 2 and 4: an earth electrode is one method but making the point TT is a separate option, and the DC-detecting device goes with a Type A or F RCD.
